title: The Spirit of truth (John 16:1–15)
hook: the Advocate will guide you into all truth

segments.voice: Yesterday, a warning with no fine print. Your line was it hated me first. Were you able to stay kind to someone cold? Day six hundred thirty-seven.

Picture a courtroom in the ancient world. You've been accused, and you're standing alone. Then someone walks in and stands beside you. Not the judge. Not a hired gun who talks over you. A friend of good standing who comes alongside and speaks up for you. The Greeks had a word for that person. Jesus has just told his friends that the world may turn against them. Now he tells them who will be standing beside them when it does.

The word is parakletos. Para means beside, and kletos means called: one called to your side. In a courtroom, that's an advocate. The King James Bible translates it Comforter, which in older English carried the sense of strengthening, from the Latin for strong. Other translations say Helper, Counselor, Advocate. No single English word holds it all, and that's why many people simply say Paraclete. Here's the surprising part. Jesus tells his friends it's good that he's leaving. "It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you." Expedient means better for you. They can't imagine that. Then he admits something tender: "I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now." He doesn't dump everything on them at once. And then the promise in today's carry: "when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth." Guide. The Greek pictures someone leading the way along a road. Not dropping all the answers at once, but walking you there. Christians understand this promise in several ways. Catholic and Orthodox Christians see the Spirit guiding the whole church through its teaching and tradition over the centuries. Many Protestants emphasize the Spirit opening the scriptures to believers as they read. Pentecostal Christians speak of the Spirit's guidance as close and present, in daily life. All of them hear it as a promise that they are not left alone to work things out. Let's look back. This week: many rooms, show us the Father, my peace, the vine, called friends, a warning, and now the Advocate.
screen: `IT IS BETTER FOR YOU THAT I GO.`
then, large: `HE WILL GUIDE YOU INTO ALL TRUTH.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: ask for guidance on one decision. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one choice in front of you right now, large or small. Don't try to solve it. Just hold it, the way you'd hold a map before a walk. Notice what you already know. Notice what you can't bear to know yet. If you pray, you can ask the Spirit to lead you one step on the road, not the whole way at once. If you don't, simply ask yourself what the next honest step would be. The bell holds the time.
Advocate. Parakletos in Greek: one called to your side, the Spirit Jesus promises will guide his friends into all truth.
Your line: into all truth. Today, take one step on the decision you held, and leave the rest of the road for later. Day six hundred thirty-seven, and another week on the path.

screen: `DAY 637 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: I HAVE OVERCOME THE WORLD.`

howItsDone: Christians often pray for the Holy Spirit's guidance before decisions, meetings and the reading of scripture, and many churches celebrate the Spirit's coming at Pentecost, fifty days after Easter.

original.note: Greek: one called alongside. a legal advocate, a helper, a counselor. the KJV says Comforter.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Comforter is someone who makes you feel better.
what it means: an advocate who stands beside you, and a guide who leads you into truth a step at a time.
what a scholar hears: parakletos, a word with a legal ring, found only in John's writings in the New Testament (John 14–16 and 1 John 2:1).
